name: PerLTQA
ontology_notes: Eval of personal long-term memory QA for 30 fictional characters, not a memory engine. Semantic memory is profiles and social relationships. Episodic memory is events and dialogues. Table 2 also lists 141 character profiles, 1,339 relationship descriptions (50 categories, 9.5 per character), 4,501 events, 3,409 event-related dialogs (25,256 utterances), and 8,593 QA pairs with 23,697 memory anchors (anchors annotated for those 30 characters). The protocol classifies the question's memory type, retrieves, then synthesizes an answer. User modeled is a character-as-person, not a companion talking to a user. Metric scores classify/retrieve/synthesize QA. Misses holes 1 identity drift after 50+ sessions, 2 socially wrong timing, 3 joke-as-fact, 4 retcon vs lie, 5 cross-character leak on one backend, 6 lore vs lived event, 7 poisoning, 8 cost per turn, 9 forget-that, 10 three-month reunion.

supersession.evidence: Tasks are classify, retrieve, and synthesize. No knowledge-update or contradiction-replace category. Du et al. SIGHAN 2024 §3.5 and §4.
supersession.label: measured

temporal.evidence: Episodic items are events and dated-looking dialogs. The scored task is still retrieve-then-answer, not last-Tuesday queries or a three-month reunion.
temporal.label: measured

identity_split.evidence: Named memory classes split profile, social relationship, event, and dialogue for one character. Thirty QA personas are separate bags, not two companions sharing one backend. Table 1 and Table 2.
identity_split.label: measured

silence.evidence: No abstention or do-not-recall items. Synthesis always answers from retrieved memories.
silence.label: measured

poisoning.evidence: Incorrect Retrieval (IR) in Table 6 is a noisy-retrieve ablation, not a stored jailbreak that later overwrites a system persona.
poisoning.label: measured

forgetting.evidence: No forget-that items. Memories are a static database for QA.
forgetting.label: measured

cost_shape.evidence: Table 5 reports average retrieval time T(s). BM25 0.030s, Contriever 0.070s, DPR 2.960s. That is retriever wall time, not cost per companion turn as session count grows.
cost_shape.label: measured

local.evidence: Dataset and code on GitHub. LICENSE.txt and README say CC BY-NC 4.0. Synthesis and judging use gpt-3.5-turbo. GitHub SPDX is NOASSERTION.
local.label: measured

companion_fit_reason: Closest public ontology among QA evals. Semantic versus episodic plus social relationships. Still classify-retrieve-synthesize. A winner can fail identity drift, silence, poisoning, forget-that, and cross-character leak.

published_eval.name: PerLTQA
published_eval.claimed_score: Table 4. BERT-base weighted precision 95.96%, recall 95.64%, F1 95.74%, accuracy 95.64% on memory classification. Table 5. BM25 R@1 0.705, DPR R@5 0.919. Table 6. gpt-3.5-turbo correct-retrieval MAP 0.842 and correctness 0.609 versus no-retrieval MAP 0.156 and correctness 0.088.
published_eval.what_it_actually_scores: Whether a classifier tags the question's memory type, a retriever returns the gold memory, and an LLM answer contains the memory anchors. Fact QA on a personal memory database. Not companion identity, silence, or poisoning.

open_unknowns: Abstract says 8,593 questions for 30 characters. Table 2 lists 141 character profiles. Anchors were annotated for 30 characters. Using both numbers.
